company.name: DIY Accounting Limited
company.registeredOffice: 37 Sutherland Avenue, Leeds, LS8 1BY, United Kingdom
company.boilerplate: DIY Accounting Limited is a family company, registered in England and Wales. Its founder, Terry Cartwright, a Chartered Management Accountant, started designing its accounting spreadsheets in 2006. It makes DIY Accounting Spreadsheets, free Excel bookkeeping and accounts workbooks for UK small businesses; DIYA-GL, which opens those books free in the browser; and DIY Accounting Submit, which files VAT returns with HMRC and company accounts with Companies House.
company.founderShort: Terry Cartwright founded DIY Accounting. A Chartered Management Accountant (ACMA) and Chartered Company Secretary (ACIS), he began designing payroll and accounting systems on Excel spreadsheets in 2006, and he designed all of its accounting and payroll software himself. Terry passed away in December 2009, and his children now manage the company.
company.founderLong: Terry Cartwright founded DIY Accounting. He qualified as a Chartered Management Accountant (ACMA) in 1971 and designed a revenue budgeting system for British Rail. He was Management and Works Accountant at New World Gas Cookers, then qualified as a Chartered Company Secretary (ACIS). At British Steel he became Head of Finance and Administration for the Refractories division. He worked in Saudi Arabia as Chief Accountant for an American corporation, then as Chief Accountant at Dunlop Industrial Hose. In the early 1980s he started his own retail and wholesale company, with turnover approaching £1 million. In the 1990s he returned to accountancy and served as Finance Director for a communications company. In 2006 he started DIY Accounting, designing payroll and accounting systems on Excel spreadsheets. As a Chartered Company Secretary he also acted as a company formation agent. Terry passed away in December 2009, and his children now manage the company.
company.team: DIY Accounting Limited is managed by the family of its founder, Terry Cartwright. The four current directors are Samantha, Jane, Antony and Lindsey Cartwright. Since January 2010 they have run the company day to day, and they keep the ease of use and the personal customer service that Terry established.

listingProducts.long:
DIY Accounting Spreadsheets are Excel workbooks for the bookkeeping and accounts of UK small businesses. A Chartered Management Accountant, Terry Cartwright, designed them, and the family company he founded has made them since 2006.

There is a package for each kind of business. Basic Sole Trader is for a sole trader who is not VAT registered and has no employees. Self Employed covers anyone self-employed, VAT registered or not, with or without employees. Company Accounts is for a limited company and uses double-entry bookkeeping. Taxi Driver, also called Cabsmart, is for taxi and private hire drivers, van drivers and couriers. Payslips prints payslips for a small employer.

Each workbook holds the spreadsheets that its business needs: sales and purchases, and where they apply cash and bank reconciliation, VAT returns, the profit and loss account, the balance sheet, final accounts and the tax figures. The totals add up as the entries go in.

Each download is one accounting period, so a business picks the year end that matches its accounts. The workbooks work in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc, come with step-by-step guides, and are free to download, funded by voluntary donations. A VAT-registered business can send its VAT return from the workbook with DIY Accounting Submit, and DIYA-GL opens the same books in a browser.

listingProducts.long:
Basic Sole Trader is the simplest package of DIY Accounting Spreadsheets. It is made for a sole trader who is not VAT registered and has no employees, and who wants to keep the books in Excel without learning double-entry bookkeeping.

The workbook holds a sales spreadsheet and a purchases spreadsheet. Each sale and each purchase goes on one row, with its date, its amount and its heading, and the totals for each month and for the year add up as the entries go in. A purchases-paid sheet records when each bill was paid, and a fixed assets sheet records equipment that the business buys.

From those entries the workbook produces a profit and loss account for the year, the figures for the short self-employed tax return, and an income tax calculation, so the sole trader can see what tax the year is likely to bring.

Each download is one accounting period, so the sole trader picks the year end that matches the accounts. The workbook works in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc and comes with a step-by-step guide. It is free to download and funded by voluntary donations. It was designed by a Chartered Management Accountant, and DIY Accounting Limited, a family company, has made it since 2006. The same books open in a browser with DIYA-GL.

listingProducts.description160: A free Excel accounts workbook for anyone self-employed, VAT registered or not: sales, purchases, bank, VAT returns, profit and loss and tax returns.
listingProducts.description500: Self Employed is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for anyone self-employed, VAT registered or not, with or without employees. It covers sales and sales invoices, purchases, cash and bank reconciliation, quarterly VAT returns, the profit and loss account and payslips. It produces the figures for both the short and the full self-employed tax return. It works in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc and is free to download.
listingProducts.long:
Self Employed is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for anyone who works for themselves, whether VAT registered or not, and with or without employees. It keeps the whole year's books in one Excel workbook.

The workbook holds a sales spreadsheet and sales invoices, a purchases spreadsheet, and a cash and bank reconciliation that checks the books against the bank statement. Each entry goes on one row with its date, its amount and its heading, and the totals add up as the entries go in.

For a VAT-registered business, the workbook produces the quarterly VAT return figures from the same entries, and DIY Accounting Submit can send that return to HMRC under Making Tax Digital. For any business, it produces the profit and loss account and the figures for both the short and the full self-employed tax return. A payslips sheet covers a business with employees.

Each download is one accounting period, so the business picks the year end that matches its accounts. The workbook works in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc and comes with a step-by-step guide. It is free to download and funded by voluntary donations. It was designed by a Chartered Management Accountant, and DIY Accounting Limited, a family company, has made it since 2006.

listingProducts.oneLine: Income, expenses, mileage and the self-employed tax return for taxi drivers, free in Excel.
listingProducts.description160: A free Excel bookkeeping workbook for taxi and private hire drivers, van drivers and couriers. It picks the cheaper of mileage or running costs.
listingProducts.description500: Taxi Driver, also called Cabsmart, is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for self-employed taxi and private hire drivers, van drivers and couriers. Record income and expenses, and the workbook compares the mileage allowance with your real vehicle running costs and uses the method that saves more tax. It produces the profit and loss account, the self-employed tax return figures and an income tax estimate. It is free to download.
listingProducts.long:
Taxi Driver, also called Cabsmart, is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for self-employed taxi drivers and private hire drivers, and also for van drivers and couriers. It keeps a driver's books for the year in one Excel workbook.

The driver records income and expenses under the headings that a driver's work has. The workbook then makes the choice that matters most for a driver's tax: it compares the mileage allowance with the real running costs of the vehicle and uses whichever method gives the larger claim. A fixed assets sheet works out the capital allowances on the vehicle and other equipment.

From those entries the workbook produces the profit and loss account, the figures for the self-employed tax return, and an estimate of the income tax for the year, so the driver can put money aside for it.

Each download is one accounting period, so the driver picks the year end that matches the accounts. The workbook works in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc and comes with a step-by-step guide. It is free to download and funded by voluntary donations. It was designed by a Chartered Management Accountant, and DIY Accounting Limited, a family company, has made it since 2006. A driver who is VAT registered can send the VAT return with DIY Accounting Submit, and DIYA-GL opens the same books in a browser.

listingProducts.long:
Company Accounts is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for a limited company, whether VAT registered or not, and with or without employees. It keeps the company's books for the year in Excel with double-entry bookkeeping.

The workbook holds a sales spreadsheet and sales invoices, a purchases spreadsheet, and a cash and bank reconciliation that checks the books against the bank statements. A fixed assets sheet works out the capital allowances, and the payslips cover 5, 10 or 20 employees.

From those entries the workbook produces the quarterly VAT returns, the monthly and yearly profit and loss account, the balance sheet, the final accounts for Companies House, and the CT600 Corporation Tax calculation. DIY Accounting Submit can send the VAT return to HMRC under Making Tax Digital and file the micro-entity or small company accounts with Companies House.

Each download is one accounting period, so the company picks the year end that matches its accounts. The workbook works in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc and comes with a step-by-step guide. It is free to download and funded by voluntary donations. It was designed by a Chartered Management Accountant who was also a Chartered Company Secretary, and DIY Accounting Limited, a family company, has made it since 2006. DIYA-GL opens the same books in a browser.

listingProducts.tagline: Free payslip spreadsheet for small employers
listingProducts.oneLine: Weekly or monthly payslips on plain paper from your PAYE figures, free in Excel.
listingProducts.description160: A free Excel payslip workbook for small employers who use a PAYE tax calculator: weekly or monthly payslips on plain paper, for 5 or 10 employees.
listingProducts.description500: Payslips is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for small employers who work out tax and National Insurance with a separate calculator, such as HMRC's Basic PAYE Tools. Enter those figures and the workbook prints weekly or monthly payslips on plain paper, with a running total of wages and deductions through the year. There are versions for 5 or 10 employees. It is free to download.
listingProducts.long:
Payslips is the DIY Accounting Spreadsheets package for a small employer who works out each employee's tax and National Insurance with a separate calculator, such as HMRC's Basic PAYE Tools, and needs payslips to hand to the employees.

The employer enters the figures that the calculator gives for each pay day: the gross pay, the tax, the National Insurance and any other deductions. The workbook then prints a payslip for each employee on plain paper, weekly or monthly, with no special stationery.

It keeps a running total of each employee's wages and deductions through the tax year, so the year-to-date figures on each payslip stay right and the employer can check the totals against the calculator at the year end. There are two versions, one for up to 5 employees and one for up to 10 employees. The Company Accounts package holds payslips for up to 20 employees beside the company's books.

Each download covers one tax year. The workbook works in Microsoft Excel and OpenOffice Calc and comes with a step-by-step guide. It is free to download and funded by voluntary donations. It was designed by a Chartered Management Accountant, and DIY Accounting Limited, a family company, has made payroll and accounting spreadsheets since 2006.

listingProducts.name: DIYA-GL
listingProducts.priceNote: No account needed. Signed in, the 35-day sandbox keeps books for 35 days after each save.
listingProducts.tagline: Your books, free in the browser
listingProducts.oneLine: Open your Basic Sole Trader, Self Employed, Taxi Driver or Limited Company books, free in your browser.
listingProducts.description160: DIYA-GL opens your Basic Sole Trader, Self Employed, Taxi Driver or Limited Company books, free in your browser.
listingProducts.description500: DIYA-GL opens your Basic Sole Trader, Self Employed, Taxi Driver or Limited Company books, free in your browser. With no account, your books stay on your device, and you can download the file to keep it. Sign in and the 35-day sandbox keeps your books for 35 days after each save, on any device. It comes from the family company behind DIY Accounting Spreadsheets and DIY Accounting Submit.
listingProducts.long:
DIYA-GL is bookkeeping in the browser, from the family company that makes DIY Accounting Spreadsheets. It opens the same four kinds of books as the spreadsheets: Basic Sole Trader, Self Employed, Taxi Driver and Limited Company.

A book can start new, or open from a DIY Accounting workbook, a zip of workbooks or a saved book file. Nothing is uploaded to open it: the file stays on the device. The book opens as sheets, as the workbook has them, and DIYA-GL works out its totals again from the entries. Where a figure read from a workbook differs from the figure that DIYA-GL works out, it shows the difference as a pencil correction, so a mistake in the workbook can be found.

With no account, the books stay on the device until the browser data is cleared, and the book downloads as a file to keep for good. Signed in, the 35-day sandbox keeps the books for 35 days after each save, on any device.

DIYA-GL is free. A VAT-registered business can fill its VAT return in DIY Accounting Submit from a DIYA-GL book, and DIYA-GL's own MCP server lets an AI assistant read a book. It is made by DIY Accounting Limited, a family company that has made accounting spreadsheets since 2006.

listingProducts.description500: DIY Accounting Limited is a family company. Our founder, Terry Cartwright, started designing our accounting spreadsheets in 2006. We make DIY Accounting Spreadsheets, free Excel bookkeeping and accounts workbooks for UK small businesses; DIYA-GL, which opens those books free in your browser; and DIY Accounting Submit, which files VAT returns with HMRC and company accounts with Companies House.
listingProducts.long:
DIY Accounting Limited is a family company, registered in England and Wales, that makes bookkeeping and filing software for UK small businesses. Its founder, Terry Cartwright, was a Chartered Management Accountant and a Chartered Company Secretary. He began designing payroll and accounting systems on Excel spreadsheets in 2006, and he answered customers' questions himself. His children have run the company since January 2010, with the same aim of ease of use and personal customer service.

The company makes three products. DIY Accounting Spreadsheets are free Excel workbooks for sole traders, the self-employed, limited companies and taxi drivers, with a payslip workbook for small employers. DIYA-GL opens those same books free in a browser, with nothing uploaded, and keeps them in a 35-day sandbox for a signed-in user.

DIY Accounting Submit files returns from the figures a business already keeps. It sends VAT returns to HMRC under Making Tax Digital, and files micro-entity and small company accounts and the confirmation statement with Companies House. It is listed on HMRC's software finder for Making Tax Digital VAT.

The products work together. A DIY Accounting workbook or a DIYA-GL book fills the VAT return in Submit, and the Company Accounts workbook produces the year-end accounts that Submit files. The spreadsheets and DIYA-GL are free, funded by voluntary donations, and Submit is a low monthly or yearly subscription.
